answer.generated: Parameter sharing in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) allows the same set of weights to be applied across different spatial locations within an image, which facilitates efficient feature extraction. This property enables the network to recognize features such as edges and textures regardless of their position in the image, thus reducing the number of parameters needed and improving generalization. In contrast, fully connected layers require separate weights for every input feature, making them less efficient and scalable for high-dimensional data like images.
